programmes.d: Magical ambition shows its dark side when Harvey drops out of school to become an industrial tycoon.
Mr. Kraft’s ex-wife returns to win him back, but Zelda isn’t going to let him go without a fight.
Purchasing a fake ID in the Other Realm causes Sabrina’s magic to become fake as well.
Mo agrees to go to another school’s prom with the son of Frank’s friend so she will no longer be busted.
Mo’s new school’s annual fund-raiser conflicts with Crenshaw High’s final summer blowout “Freaknik”, and Frank and Dee insist Mo should attend the fund-raiser.
Moesha tries to get sympathy from her visiting grandfather over having to go to a new school.
Mo attends the first day at her new school and is miserable. She has only made one friend and feels out of place.
Hakeem begins to date an older woman he meets at his store.
Dee wins a free decorating consultation at Mo’s school raffle and can’t wait to redo the house.
Mo writes a scene from a play set in a Blues Lounge in the 1940s for her English class, and our cast acts it out for us.
Mo tells her friends at the Den that Hayley’s dad is an important record executive.
Brent panics over hair loss, worsened by Lacey. Wanda's lamp is in demand. Hank's bad at fixing appliances.
Lacey's newsletter and Brent's cartoons cause drama. Oscar's paper route nightmare.
Brent faces Emma's traditional Christmas. Lacey's trip home is disrupted. Hank's gift drive goes wrong.
Hank exposes Lacey's rude friend. Brent and Wanda manage a rewards card chaos.
Hank struggles to build a Lego Dog River. Wanda's birthday avoidance works too well.
Brent and Lacey compete to keep secrets from Karen. Wanda is denied a credit card, while Hank gets approved.
Brent fixates on the door repairman. Wanda guards her telescope. Oscar and Emma's RV trip annoys everyone.
Brent's jellybean contest to save the park goes awry. Hank lies about a Lamborghini.
Appa worries about Umma after a minor household accident. Janet uses Jung's past to boost her reputation with students. A high school reunion has Kimchee thinking about an old flame.
Appa's reputation as an impartial umpire faces a stiff test. Jung and Kimchee disagree about discipline. Janet worries a sweater may be haunted.
Kimchee's plan to impress the higher-ups backfires. Shannon inadvertently insults Umma's cooking. Appa and Janet enter a prank war.
Umma tries to set up Janet with their new mason. Shannon encourages Jung to give Appa a gift. Kimchee and Shannon work on employee evaluations.
Janet and Appa take a first aid course. Umma worries her prayers cause more harm than good. Shannon and Jung discuss their relationship.
Jung gives Appa and Umma a business presentation for the store. Shannon and Kimchee's office teasing leads to a meaningful discovery for Kimchee.
As Victoria interviews the governor's candidly opportunistic wife, Elka goes on trial and attempts to sway the verdict by flirting with an elderly juror.

Elka's on the lam and the women go looking for her…in Amish country. Meanwhile, Joy's a source of scandal as the Governor's alleged mistress and faces deportation while Victoria finds herself a little too "at home" with the Amish.
The women are terrified that an ex-con Victoria deceived will show up at the house, and Joy finally meets her son Owen, who thinks it may be best not to stay in contact.
After getting each other dates for another shared fake birthday, the women's night involves a Jesus look-alike, Siamese twins, an impressionist, and an astute waiter.
While rehearsing for a battle of the bands, Rick poaches away talented lead singer Joy, leaving Melanie, Victoria and Elka no choice but to use autotune microphones.
Joy learns from a fertility clinic director that Rick is their most sought-after donor, and Victoria method-acts as an old woman to land a prestigious stage role.
Looking for "GBFFs" like they had in L.A., the women go to a gay bar, where Victoria is mistaken for a drag queen, and Elka punches out her former best friend.
Victoria tries to convince her daughter Emmy not to release a tell-all book, while Melanie and Joy are screened by a kid to be his father's new wife.

Things take a literal turn for the worse when a license-less Chris volunteers to move his dad's car, but finds himself driving the car all the way to school as a result of trying to impress Tasha. Rochelle spends an interesting day at traffic court.
As a result of their apartment being broken into, Julius and Rochelle decide it's a good idea to get a dog, something Chris has always wanted.
With no extracurricular activities to his name, Chris decides to join the writing staff of the school newspaper.
